_meta.what: The level-skip specimens the adversarial suite fires against. Charter D12: the ratified table at /papers/survey-once-build-forever has SIX rows, not seven. Unratified specimens are present but labelled UNCAUGHT with a reason, because labelling the gap honestly is the anti-vacuity discipline — padding the fixture by pretending the grammar catches them is the same laundering the epic exists to prevent.

authority_hierarchy.L1: running system — served bytes, live DB, box HEAD, a real click
authority_hierarchy.L3: local checkout — a CLAIM about L2
authority_hierarchy.L4: generated artifacts — openapi.json, token layer, goldens
authority_hierarchy.L5: charters / docs / cards — a CLAIM about L2
authority_hierarchy.L6: agent memory / the wish — a CLAIM about L5

rules.R1: a fact records the level it was read at and may never be quoted above it
rules.R2: a fact records its DEPENDENCIES, not just its subject
rules.R3: no fact is stored without a demonstration the method COULD have answered differently — rejection at WRITE time
rules.R4: conflicting facts are BOTH stored and flagged, never resolved by write order

_meta.caught_by_is_a_hypothesis: Every `caught_by` label below is a HYPOTHESIS for the acceptance suite (slice 6) to TEST, never a verified fact. This fixture's own gate checks its STRUCTURE, not its semantics: a specimen labelled R1 that R1 does not actually catch passes here and fails only in slice 6. Reading these labels as measured catches would be the level-skip this fixture documents, committed against the fixture itself.
_meta.freeze_doctrine: Freeze the COMMAND and the identity of what was read (sha, ref, host). Never freeze a measured number as a standing assertion — numbers drift, and a frozen number encodes a fact that may already be false. Where a specimen names a figure, it is recorded as an observation WITH its observed_at, never as an assertion.
_meta.rerun_verification: Every `rerun` below was executed on 2026-07-20 from a clean worktree; `last_rerun` records what it returned. Re-run them — do not trust these transcripts.

row_count_provenance.why_this_matters: Accepting 'six rows' from the brief would have been an L6 read quoted as an L5 fact about the paper — this fixture's own failure mode, committed while building the fixture that documents it. The count is derived from the paper, not from the prompt.

_meta.r3_has_no_check_on_the_fact_path: MEASURED 2026-09-02, and recorded here so it cannot decay into folklore. R3 is enforced NOWHERE on the fact path. admitFact's entire rejection vocabulary is MISSING-SUBJECT, MISSING-CLAIM, BAD-DEPS, LEVEL-SKIP, PATHLESS-REF and INADMISSIBLE-CONTINUOUS, and not one of them asks whether the method could have answered differently; adjudicate composes that vocabulary and adds none of its own. R3 lives only in the injected `now`/`screen` bounds admitRecipe takes on the RECIPE path. It is unenforceable at the fact seam as the record is shaped: the eight fields a fact carries are subject, quantity, claim, evidence, rerun, level, observed_at and deps, and NONE of them can hold a negative demonstration. `evidence` is the only field that could carry the prose of one, and it is L6 by construction and never parsed (D1, whose prose-scanner precursor scored 0.67 precision) — so a check keyed on it would be keyed on nothing. Closing R3 here needs a fact-SHAPE decision (a `control` field holding a literal COMMAND, which the grammar could level and screen the way it already levels `rerun`), not a new branch in admitFact. Specimen 103 is the standing negative control for the gap: it violates R3 with honest levels and the adjudicator ADMITS it.

specimens.title: deploy lag: "0, the fix is live"
specimens.level_skip: read at L2 (git HEAD matched origin/main), claimed at L1 ("it is live")
specimens.wrong_evidence: deploy lag: 0, the fix is live
specimens.honest_counterpart: origin/main contains the fix (L2). Whether the running BEAM has rebuilt to it is a SEPARATE L1 question, answered only by asking the box.
specimens.rerun: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 -i ~/.ssh/barkpark_indx root@157.180.90.121 'cd /opt/barkpark && git rev-parse --short HEAD'
specimens.why_caught: The L2 command (`git rev-parse origin/main`) derives level L2. The claim asserts L1. R1 forbids quoting a fact above the level its command derives, so the claim is rejected without anyone needing to know the right answer.

lag.description: The control FIRING: the box is behind origin/main, so an L2 read would have forged a false L1 claim.
lag.note: Observed as 11 behind earlier in the session and 13 at freeze time. The lag is a MOVING observation, never a frozen assertion — re-run `git rev-list --count <box_head>..origin/main` to re-derive.
lag.rerun_lag_count: git rev-list --count $(ssh -o BatchMode=yes -i ~/.ssh/barkpark_indx root@157.180.90.121 'cd /opt/barkpark && git rev-parse HEAD')..origin/main

no_lag.description: The control NOT firing: box HEAD equals origin/main. The level-skip is still a level-skip — the L2 read simply happened to agree with L1 this time. This side is frozen so the specimen does not depend on the lag persisting; an auto-deploy can close it within the hour.
no_lag.synthetic_note: CONSTRUCTED, not observed. The lag side was captured live; this side was hand-written because the box WAS behind at freeze time, so an equal-HEAD observation did not exist to capture. box_head and origin_main below are PLACEHOLDER STRINGS, not shas — any consumer that reads them as commit ids is reading fiction. The side exists to pin the ASSERTION (reject the L1 claim even when the answer agrees), never to supply data.
no_lag.note: A correct answer reached by an inadmissible method is still inadmissible. The suite must reject the L1 claim in BOTH sides — a grammar that only rejects when the answer happens to be wrong is grading the answer, not the method.

specimens.note_on_corroboration: Three agents agreeing is NOT independent confirmation when they share a root cause (one stale checkout). This specimen is also the R2 case: the fact's real dependency is the checkout's freshness, not the file.

specimens.title: "64.00ch at viewport 900" vs 44.80ch under a panel
specimens.level_skip: NONE — this is a unit/identity confusion WITHIN one level: two different measurements of two different things, both read at L1, reported as one quantity.
specimens.verified_row_text: "64.00ch at viewport 900" | the layout box | the reader's eye, which saw 44.80ch under a panel
specimens.verified_row_note: The ratified row itself names no L-levels for this specimen — its two columns are 'the layout box' and 'the reader's eye', not L-numbers. That is the paper agreeing, in its own wording, that this row is not a level-skip. Confirms the UNCAUGHT label is faithful to the source rather than a builder's convenience.
specimens.wrong_evidence: measured line length is 64.00ch at viewport 900
specimens.honest_counterpart: The two figures measure different viewport conditions (unoccluded vs occluded by an inspector panel). Neither is wrong; naming them as one quantity is. The correct record names the occlusion axis as a DEPENDENCY of the measurement.
specimens.rerun_note: This re-derives the IDENTITY of the served artifact whose typography was measured, not the measurement. Re-measuring requires driving a real browser at a declared viewport AND a declared occlusion state; the measurement command is the browser run, and its two inputs must both be named or the figure is meaningless.
specimens.why_no_number: The figures have ALREADY drifted to 44.69 / 37.9 and the occlusion moved from the `default` to the `user-opened` inspector axis. Freezing 64.00 would encode a fact that is already false — the fixture would ship a lie as its own control. Charter doctrine: freeze the served_sha and the command, never the number.
specimens.uncaught_reason: R1 compares the level a fact was READ at against the level it is CLAIMED at. Both figures here were read at L1 and claimed at L1, so R1 has nothing to compare and structurally cannot fire. Catching this needs R2 (the measurement's DEPENDENCIES — viewport and occlusion — must be recorded as part of the fact) plus D7's discrete-predicate rule. Recorded as a known gap in the wave-1 grammar, NOT as a caught case.

last_rerun.note: L1 and L3 agreed at freeze time. Agreement is an OBSERVATION, not a licence to read L3 and claim L1 next time — see specimen 1's no_lag side.

specimens.wrong_evidence: ops recipient is configured: kalle@jarl.no is set and the config parses

The R3 hypothesis was never ratified — the paper's row names no rule and no L-levels (see verified_row_text) — and it was REFUTED by running the specimen through the real adjudicator: R3 has no check on the fact path at all (see _meta.r3_has_no_check_on_the_fact_path). A label naming a rule that does not exist where the fact is admitted is this fixture's own subject matter committed against the fixture, so the label now names the rule that fires and the R3 content is kept below as an OBSERVATION rather than deleted.
specimens.why_caught: The read is L5/L3 and the claim is L1, so the derived level is a ceiling BELOW the claimed level and LEVEL-SKIP fires on admission, before any other reasoning. Measured, not assumed: `node tooling/grip/acceptance.mjs` reports this specimen REJECTED (LEVEL-SKIP), and L5 is remapped to L3 in the report because no command derives L5.
specimens.r3_observation: The specimen IS also an R3 violation and that stays true: the check would have reported success against an empty list just as readily, so nothing demonstrated the method could have answered differently. That is an OBSERVATION about the specimen, never a catch — and it can never be the catch here, because R1 fires first on a fact whose levels are dishonest. Specimen 103 is the same violation with HONEST levels, which is the only shape an R3 check could ever be tested on.

specimens.title: `emit --write` reporting success
specimens.level_skip: read at L4 (the generated region regenerated cleanly), claimed at L2/L3 ("the file is correct")
specimens.wrong_evidence: emit --write succeeded, the artifacts are in sync
specimens.honest_counterpart: The generated region regenerated cleanly AND the write deleted 33 authored lines outside that region. A generator reporting success speaks only for what it generates; it is silent about what it destroyed.
specimens.rerun_note: The BARE invocation is check mode — it does not write. Verified 0.11s, green, 19 artifacts in sync on 2026-07-20.
specimens.why_caught: The generator's own exit code is an L4 fact about generated regions. Claiming file-level correctness is an L2/L3 claim about the whole file, including authored regions the generator never inspected. R1 rejects the promotion.
specimens.dependency_note: Also an R2 case: the fact's real dependency is the set of lines OUTSIDE the generated region, which the L4 read never touched.

specimens.title: "census.mjs never screens" — a grep that could not see the file
specimens.level_skip: NONE — read at L3 (a local grep over a local file) and claimed at L3 (a statement about that same local file). The two levels are EQUAL, so R1 has nothing to compare and structurally cannot fire. What failed is the CONTROL, not the ladder.
specimens.wrong_evidence: census.mjs never screens a command — grep found no occurrences of the screen call in it
specimens.honest_counterpart: The file carried a literal NUL byte, so the shell's grep wrapper skipped it as binary and printed nothing at exit 1 — byte-identical to `no matches`. `/usr/bin/grep -ac census tooling/grip/census.mjs` returns 30 on the same file. The read could never have come back non-empty, so an empty result distinguished nothing: it measured the wrapper, not the file. The verifier who drew this concluded the exact opposite of the truth and caught it by accident.
specimens.rerun_note: The honest counterpart, not the sin: `-a` forces the binary-safe read the bare wrapper refused. The sinful command is the wrapper form the specimen's prose describes, which is why it is not the `rerun` field — the same asymmetry the ratified specimens carry.
specimens.uncaught_reason: R1 compares the level a fact was READ at against the level it is CLAIMED at; both are L3 here, so R1 structurally cannot fire — the fact is honestly levelled and WRONG. Catching it is exactly R3's job (`no fact is stored without a demonstration the method COULD have answered differently`), and R3 has NO check on the fact path: run this specimen through the real adjudicator and it comes back ADMITTED with zero reasons. Recorded as a known gap, NOT as a catch.
specimens.control_that_should_have_run: Run the same wrapper against a file the pattern is KNOWN to occur in and assert a non-zero count BEFORE trusting the zero. If that positive control cannot fail, an empty result is not an absence — it is an unread file.
specimens.why_frozen_anyway: Frozen as the fixture's FIRST R3-shaped specimen and as an explicit negative control. Specimen 5 was labelled R3 for a year and could never have tested R3, because its levels are dishonest and LEVEL-SKIP fires first — so no R3 check was testable against the fixture at all. This specimen supplies the missing shape: an R3 violation R1 cannot reach. The suite must NOT claim to catch it while the fact path has no R3 check, and the day one lands, the assertion that this specimen is ADMITTED goes red and this label gets re-derived — which is the whole point of freezing it.
specimens.why_this_one: It is real and it happened inside this module. tooling/grip/README.md records it under its own METHOD RULING: every negative in the epic resting on grepping census.mjs through the wrapper is VOID. A fixture of invented sins would be the vacuity this epic exists to prevent.
